response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT a.player_id, p.death_country, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON p.player_id = a.player_id WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL GROUP BY a.player_id, p.death_country), av AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS m FROM t) SELECT SUM(t.total) AS sum_of_totals, AVG(t.total - av.m) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM t CROSS JOIN av WHERE t.total > av.m

assumptions.assumption: Players are inner-joined to player, which has one row per player_id. Players with a NULL death_country (for example, living players) are still included, because the request does not say to exclude them. The average total is taken over all matched players.
The average total is the unweighted mean of the per-player totals, not of the individual appearance rows.
The 'average amount by which they exceed that average' is the mean of (total - average total) over the kept players.
